commit_message:
[Codegen][LLVMCPU] Split loadProcessorData: hoist only the alloca (#24786)

35b2070 (#24749) fixed unbounded stack growth by moving the whole
loadProcessorData CPU-feature patch buffer construction to the function
entry block. But that also hoisted the feature-bit or/store away from
the ukernel call, and once the ukernel inlines, LLVM can no longer
store-to-load forward the forced feature bits into the ukernel's runtime
feature check across the enclosing loop, so the mmt4d/pack tile-func
select never devirtualizes and the microkernel is left out-of-line.

Split the two concerns: reserve only the alloca (the stack slot, the
actual cause of #24744) in the entry block, but keep the feature-bit
patch at the call site. The stores re-run per iteration but allocate no
stack, so the stack stays bounded while the forced bits remain adjacent
to the (inlined) load and fold as before, restoring devirtualization.

Assisted-by: Claude-Code

commit_message:
feat(KernelDispatch): set inner-tile alignment hints on scalable pack ops

During tile size selection, when global tile sizes and mappings to each operation
are available each scalable `linalg.pack` inner tile is compared against the loop
tile size chosen for that dimension and the inner tile alignment hints
are set , before the loop tiles are translated into the packed outer domain.

A `linalg.pack` whose producer is a `linalg.unpack` is pruned by
MultiLoweringConfigGenerator  and never receives a lowering config, so it is not
it is handled separately by reading the producer unpack's per-level tile
sizes and comparing them against the pack's scalable inner tiles.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[Codegen] Support multi-output consumers with permuted indexing maps (#24768)

Extend lowering of fused & tiled consumer ops from the basic case
(strictly identical indexing over the output operands). We now
generalize the logic for input indexing to support different output maps
that are simple permutations.

This allows to support some fusion cases where a simple transposition
from one of the consumer's connections get fused into the elementwise
generic, and then the consumer gets fused & tiled together with the
matmul. Whether we want such consumer fusion is a separate matter
subject to performance investigations, and in my reproducer there'd also
be an opportunity to fold redundant `tranpose(transpose(x))` instances,
avoiding the multi-output fusion altogether. For better stability, this
extension of the codegen is preferred as the first step.

Signed-off-by: Artem Gindinson <gindinson@roofline.ai>
Assisted by: Codex

commit_message:
feat(KernelDispatch): set inner-tile alignment hints on scalable pack ops

During tile-size selection, `MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs`
compares each scalable `linalg.pack` inner tile against the loop tile size chosen
for that dimension (`getScalableInnerTileAlignment`) and stamps the per-level
result via `InnerTileAlignmentsAttr::setOnOp`, before the loop tiles are
translated into the packed outer domain (`capturePackInnerTileAlignment`).

A `linalg.pack` whose producer is a `linalg.unpack` is pruned by
`shouldSetLoweringConfig` and never receives a lowering config, so it is not
visited by `setNewTilingConfigs`. Handle it separately in
`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`: read the producer unpack's per-level tile
sizes and compare them against the pack's scalable inner tiles, stashing the same
`inner_tile_alignments` attribute.

The distribution level is intentionally skipped for now (see TODO).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: clang-tidy

commit_message:
feat(KernelDispatch): set inner-tile alignment hints on scalable unpack ops

Stacks on the scalable-pack hint support. Extend the alignment capture in
`MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs` to `linalg.unpack` ops:
after the loop tile sizes are scaled up into the unpacked (dest) domain by
`undoScaleAndPermutateTilingForUnpackOp`, each scalable inner tile is compared
against the (now scalable) loop tile on its dimension and the per-level result
is stashed as `iree_codegen.inner_tile_alignments`. This lets
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn` read the unpack's alignment back instead of
recomputing it post-mortem. Distribution level excluded (see TODO).

Stacks on the scalable-pack hint support. Extend the alignment capture in
`MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs` to `linalg.unpack` ops:
after the loop tile sizes are scaled up into the unpacked (dest) domain by
`undoScaleAndPermutateTilingForUnpackOp`, each scalable inner tile is compared
against the (now scalable) loop tile on its dimension and the per-level result
is stashed as `iree_codegen.inner_tile_alignments`. This lets
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn` read the unpack's alignment back instead of
recomputing it post-mortem. Distribution level excluded (see TODO).

commit_message:
feat(KernelDispatch): set inner-tile alignment hints on scalable pack ops

During tile-size selection, `MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs`
compares each scalable `linalg.pack` inner tile against the loop tile size chosen
for that dimension (`getScalableInnerTileAlignment`) and stamps the per-level
result via `InnerTileAlignmentsAttr::setOnOp`, before the loop tiles are
translated into the packed outer domain (`capturePackInnerTileAlignment`).

A `linalg.pack` whose producer is a `linalg.unpack` is pruned by
`shouldSetLoweringConfig` and never receives a lowering config, so it is not
visited by `setNewTilingConfigs`. Handle it separately in
`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`: read the producer unpack's per-level tile
sizes and compare them against the pack's scalable inner tiles, stashing the same
`inner_tile_alignments` attribute.

The distribution level is intentionally skipped for now (see TODO).

commit_message:
feat(KernelDispatch): set inner-tile alignment hints on scalable pack ops

During tile-size selection, `MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs`
compares each scalable `linalg.pack` inner tile against the loop tile size chosen
for that dimension (`getScalableInnerTileAlignment`) and stamps the per-level
result via `InnerTileAlignmentsAttr::setOnOp`, before the loop tiles are
translated into the packed outer domain (`capturePackInnerTileAlignment`).

A `linalg.pack` whose producer is a `linalg.unpack` is pruned by
`shouldSetLoweringConfig` and never receives a lowering config, so it is not
visited by `setNewTilingConfigs`. Handle it separately in
`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`: read the producer unpack's per-level tile
sizes and compare them against the pack's scalable inner tiles, stashing the same
`inner_tile_alignments` attribute.

The distribution level is intentionally skipped for now (see TODO).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: clang-tidy

commit_message:
feat(KernelDispatch): set inner-tile alignment hints on scalable unpack ops

Stacks on the scalable-pack hint support. Extend the alignment capture in
`MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs` to `linalg.unpack` ops:
after the loop tile sizes are scaled up into the unpacked (dest) domain by
`undoScaleAndPermutateTilingForUnpackOp`, each scalable inner tile is compared
against the (now scalable) loop tile on its dimension and the per-level result
is stashed as `iree_codegen.inner_tile_alignments`. This lets
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn` read the unpack's alignment back instead of
recomputing it post-mortem. Distribution level excluded (see TODO).

commit_message:
feat(KernelDispatch): set inner-tile alignment hints on scalable unpack ops

Stacks on the scalable-pack hint support. Extend the alignment capture in
`MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs` to `linalg.unpack` ops:
after the loop tile sizes are scaled up into the unpacked (dest) domain by
`undoScaleAndPermutateTilingForUnpackOp`, each scalable inner tile is compared
against the (now scalable) loop tile on its dimension and the per-level result
is stashed as `iree_codegen.inner_tile_alignments`. This lets
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn` read the unpack's alignment back instead of
recomputing it post-mortem. Distribution level excluded (see TODO).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[Codegen][LLVMCPU] Split loadProcessorData: hoist only the alloca (#24786)

35b2070 (#24749) fixed unbounded stack growth by moving the whole
loadProcessorData CPU-feature patch buffer construction to the function
entry block. But that also hoisted the feature-bit or/store away from
the ukernel call, and once the ukernel inlines, LLVM can no longer
store-to-load forward the forced feature bits into the ukernel's runtime
feature check across the enclosing loop, so the mmt4d/pack tile-func
select never devirtualizes and the microkernel is left out-of-line.

Split the two concerns: reserve only the alloca (the stack slot, the
actual cause of #24744) in the entry block, but keep the feature-bit
patch at the call site. The stores re-run per iteration but allocate no
stack, so the stack stays bounded while the forced bits remain adjacent
to the (inlined) load and fold as before, restoring devirtualization.

Assisted-by: Claude-Code

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Fix GatherFusionPattern on a scalar producer operand (#24803)

GatherFusionPattern builds a tensor.extract for every operand of the
producer generic, so a scalar operand reached cast<TensorType> and
asserted. A scalar is invariant over the iteration space, so there is no
index to permute and nothing to extract: the fused body reads the value
itself.

The producer has to be a bit extend or a transpose to qualify, and that
classification deliberately ignores non-tensor inputs, so a qualifying
producer can have them. A per-tensor dequantize widening i8 to f32 with
its scale passed as an f32 is one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Fix GatherFusionPattern on a scalar producer operand (#24803)

GatherFusionPattern builds a tensor.extract for every operand of the
producer generic, so a scalar operand reached cast<TensorType> and
asserted. A scalar is invariant over the iteration space, so there is no
index to permute and nothing to extract: the fused body reads the value
itself.

The producer has to be a bit extend or a transpose to qualify, and that
classification deliberately ignores non-tensor inputs, so a qualifying
producer can have them. A per-tensor dequantize widening i8 to f32 with
its scale passed as an f32 is one.

[DispatchCreation] Fix GatherFusionPattern on a scalar producer operand (#24803)

GatherFusionPattern builds a tensor.extract for every operand of the
producer generic, so a scalar operand reached cast<TensorType> and
asserted. A scalar is invariant over the iteration space, so there is no
index to permute and nothing to extract: the fused body reads the value
itself.

The producer has to be a bit extend or a transpose to qualify, and that
classification deliberately ignores non-tensor inputs, so a qualifying
producer can have them. A per-tensor dequantize widening i8 to f32 with
its scale passed as an f32 is one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[Codegen][LLVMCPU] Make cpu_data feature field a compile-time constant

The processor_data passed to a ukernel call is built with the CPU
feature bitmask set to a compile-time constant taken from the executable
target's cpu_features. The remaining fields of environment's cpu_data
(currently unused) are copied from the runtime processor data.

A constant feature field lets each ukernel's feature check fold at compile time,
so the matching tile is selected and inlined and the off-target tile variants
are DCE'd before codegen.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: pre-commit

The processor_data passed to a ukernel call is built with the CPU
feature bitmask set to a compile-time constant taken from the executable
target's cpu_features. The remaining fields of environment's cpu_data
(currently unused) are copied from the runtime processor data.

A constant feature field lets each ukernel's feature check fold at compile time,
so the matching tile is selected and inlined and the off-target tile variants
are DCE'd before codegen.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: Unit Test / Linux (x86_64)

commit_message:
[Codegen] Support multi-output consumers with permuted indexing maps (#24768)

Extend lowering of fused & tiled consumer ops from the basic case
(strictly identical indexing over the output operands). We now
generalize the logic for input indexing to support different output maps
that are simple permutations.

This allows to support some fusion cases where a simple transposition
from one of the consumer's connections get fused into the elementwise
generic, and then the consumer gets fused & tiled together with the
matmul. Whether we want such consumer fusion is a separate matter
subject to performance investigations, and in my reproducer there'd also
be an opportunity to fold redundant `tranpose(transpose(x))` instances,
avoiding the multi-output fusion altogether. For better stability, this
extension of the codegen is preferred as the first step.

Signed-off-by: Artem Gindinson <gindinson@roofline.ai>
Assisted by: Codex

commit_message:
[Codegen][LLVMCPU] Split loadProcessorData: hoist only the alloca (#24786)

35b2070 (#24749) fixed unbounded stack growth by moving the whole
loadProcessorData CPU-feature patch buffer construction to the function
entry block. But that also hoisted the feature-bit or/store away from
the ukernel call, and once the ukernel inlines, LLVM can no longer
store-to-load forward the forced feature bits into the ukernel's runtime
feature check across the enclosing loop, so the mmt4d/pack tile-func
select never devirtualizes and the microkernel is left out-of-line.

Split the two concerns: reserve only the alloca (the stack slot, the
actual cause of #24744) in the entry block, but keep the feature-bit
patch at the call site. The stores re-run per iteration but allocate no
stack, so the stack stays bounded while the forced bits remain adjacent
to the (inlined) load and fold as before, restoring devirtualization.

Assisted-by: Claude-Code

---------

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

[Codegen][LLVMCPU] Split loadProcessorData: hoist only the alloca (#24786)

35b2070 (#24749) fixed unbounded stack growth by moving the whole
loadProcessorData CPU-feature patch buffer construction to the function
entry block. But that also hoisted the feature-bit or/store away from
the ukernel call, and once the ukernel inlines, LLVM can no longer
store-to-load forward the forced feature bits into the ukernel's runtime
feature check across the enclosing loop, so the mmt4d/pack tile-func
select never devirtualizes and the microkernel is left out-of-line.

Split the two concerns: reserve only the alloca (the stack slot, the
actual cause of #24744) in the entry block, but keep the feature-bit
patch at the call site. The stores re-run per iteration but allocate no
stack, so the stack stays bounded while the forced bits remain adjacent
to the (inlined) load and fold as before, restoring devirtualization.
